I've been wanting to try out Linux for a long time now, but was always hesitant to try dual-booting for fear of ruining my Windows 7 installation. My system is a little older, and like everyone else, I always seem to be a little short on hard drive space. I have a few 2TB portable USB drives for media/data, but in terms of SATA-connected drives I only have 2 120GB SSDs. I have Windows 7 on my C:/ and used D:/ for mostly torrenting and installing games on to.

I decided after reading around a little to shrink my D:/ partition in Windows Disk Management to create 40GB of free space before starting, to avoid any shocking messages about disk integrity. I decided to try out LinuxMint 18.1 Serena with Cinnamon desktop (I'm brand new to Linux, and have heard it's rather user-friendly for beginners).

After downloading from torrent, and burning the ISO to a DVD for install, I would get nothing but a black screen every time I booted. I decided to try using a USB stick instead, and downloaded PendriveLinux to create the bootable USB drive. I still got nothing but a black screen every time. I found a few forums that said to press E or TAB instead of trying to boot, and finding where it said "quiet splash" and then adding "nomodeset", and pressing F10 to boot.

Suddenly I could load the desktop! I double-clicked the "Install LinuxMint" icon and chose the "Something Else" option. I created a primary ex4 / mount point of 10GB, a swap of 16GB, and gave the remaining 14GB to logical ex4 /home. I installed Mint in the created area, then restarted. Set my BIOS to boot my 2nd drive first, and everything looked perfect. Still got nothing but black screen after restart unless I included "nomodeset".

I tried updating all my packages/kernel/etc nothing would help. The maker of my video card didn't make drivers for LinuxMint. My video card suddenly died a few months ago, and I replaced it with the cheapest card I could at the time (an AMD RX460). I finally found the solution after hours and hours of searching and reading, completely frustrated and ready to give up.

Someone suggested that AMD had put out drivers for Ubuntu 16, and that Mint was really Ubuntu under the hood, so they worked fine. You just had to manually download the 17.xx amd-gpu-pro drivers for Ubuntu, then edit the installer to read "linuxmint" where it said "ubuntu". Then I had to update my Kernel to 4.8.xx, and install the amd-gpu-driver from the terminal.

Rebooted, and just like magic, I suddenly had a working system. Reordered my GRUB menu so that Windows will boot by default (I heard that was just a good idea, because of Windows Update).

I'm probably more pleased with myself than I ought to be, but goddamn did I ever want to give up a few times. Had to wade through 95% comments of "fuck AMD I'm just returning this card in the morning" to find anything helpful, and 95% of the advice didn't end up helping me.

I've got all the basics customized and set up, so what should I do next? What do I do with my new OS other than email people and use LibreOffice? I've never used any Linux environment other than my Android phone (and getting away from Google and MS and the rest is part of why I wanted to switch to Linux anyways).

Thanks for reading. I'd love to hear what you guys are up to on Linux.
